scope: Full intended programmable PHY companion; mathematical closure precedes transistor schematic closure and layout.

requirements.remaining: Declared candidate now combines live wired CDR/idle/supply kicks, wideband modulated RF/multipole filtering/blockers/phase events, both converter pipelines, shared reference loads and host pauses. Four signed both-mode cases pass transport and provisional RF quality. Missing intended functions elsewhere in this inventory and broader uncertainty/independent-source operation still prevent whole-chip closure. Pass848 combines the public supply-coupled detector before four-path traffic, independent wideband RF, autonomous sampled clocks, shared ADC/DAC reference loads and a16-word host pause. Both32-frame cases pass with3.785%/4.945% held-out error; this finite candidate screen does not close whole-chip uncertainty or all supported controls.

Common-reference rates and selected visibility/phase tests pass;16/64-word H2D pauses pass and256-word pauses fault. Still establish variable CDC, arbitrary service-phase and finite queue bounds across lock transients.

Standalone compliance-limited pump model qualifies40 of44 startup cases; four miss30us. All six prior ideal-current compliance boundaries recover under the assumed symmetric rolloff law. Full-chip integration, mismatch/reset delay/noise, carrier controls and independent full RF quality remain open; this is not a measured GF180 current law. Managed RF carrier tuning is now connected in the sampled-clock profile: six both-mode cases preserve oscillator phase/filter state and reacquire. Fractional ratios still use ideal average feedback; physical divider edges and tuned independent RF quality remain open. Pass861 adds isolated pulse-loop phase forecasting and connects the compliance-dependent loop to the actual wired serializer/channel at both rates. Exact word transport and non-mutating forecasts pass. Full-chip reset/reference, noise/supply and RF/fractional adapters remain open. Pass862 pulse loops now preserve phase/filter charge through reference loss, gate pump current and reacquire on reference return; four both-rate lifecycle cases and serializer regression pass. Detection delay, leakage/noise, returned reference phase and full-chip adapter remain open. Pass863 pulse loops support exact exponential rail-frequency forcing, continuous phase/filter state and live serializer retiming; four signed/both-rate cases pass with analytical and subdivision controls. Pump/reference PSRR, noise and common-chip substitution remain open. Pass864 pulse loops integrate the immutable finite-spectrum frequency-noise source exactly into phase, with independent quadrature/subdivision/forecast checks at both rates. Pump/reference noise, fractional feedback and the full-chip adapter remain open. Pass865 substitutes an integer pulse-clock service for wired timing in the common controller. Both-mode transport and opposite-mode recovery pass; RF remains sampled, and fractional/phase-step operations reject explicitly. Band-switch charge/work and RF adapter remain open. Pass866 PulseChip connects both pulse synthesizers, using unwrapped RF phase. Independent tone and simultaneous ADC/wired transport pass; assumed-noise tone error is9.82% against10% maximum budget, so margin remains weak. RF tuning rejects explicitly; wideband and recovery coverage remain open. Pass867 both-pulse combined wideband cases pass with4.87–5.91% held-out RMS error. Pass868 managed integer-channel tuning preserves phase and capacitor state and passes six both-mode tone/converter cases. Fractional feedback remains unavailable. Pass869 actual first-order fractional divider reaches mean2.412/2.437GHz but fails current lock qualification; dense timing ripple is5.39/32.15ps RMS. Arithmetic and forecast tests pass only. Fractional quality remains an explicit unresolved risk. Pass870 second-order integer feedback at500kHz bandwidth qualifies the two tested fractional channels with1.59/3.35ps RMS deterministic timing and2.41%/5.13% phase-only error. At1MHz it remains inadequate. Full-chain integration, device noise and broader ratios remain open. Pass871 full-chip fractional RF requires a longer unchanged-limit qualification window;500kHz still fails2.437GHz acquisition.350kHz qualifies both channels/modes and passes loaded-reference tone/converter/wired transport at1.10–2.91% held-out error. Device noise, wideband fractional operation and the full channel grid remain open. Pass872 the350kHz shaped candidate passes both channels/modes with assumed oscillator noise at6.40–7.64% held-out tone error. Wideband comparison must include deterministic divider distortion against an ideal tuned reference; broader noise/grid coverage remains open. Pass874/875 fractional wideband against an ideal tuned reference passes four carrier/mode cases at7.38–8.03% with20/30MHz carrier-relative blockers. Fixed-laboratory in-band interference failures remain archived. Broader channel/noise/uncertainty coverage and physical validation remain open.

Autonomous shared RF LO now drives both mixers. Independent tone reception exposes clock disturbances which cancel in loopback; four modulated external-input cases retain both converter delays and wired traffic, with uncoupled TX-isolation controls. Extend combined-profile signal-quality and uncertainty measurements to these autonomous clocks. RF gain, images/leakage and overload recovery remain open. Managed carrier tuning now passes six independent-tone analytical-response cases and two detuning controls with64-sample converter transport. This covers a noiseless single-pole tone response only; combined wideband quality remains open. Independent50-carrier reception now passes a32-frame four-path run in both modes with sampled autonomous RF/wired clocks, finite converter delays, spectral oscillator noise, host/return supply pulling and frontend impairments. Held-out incremental errors are3.95%/4.86%; blockers, wider uncertainty and actual pulse-loop integration remain open. Four both-mode/signed blocker and cubic-response cases now pass with3.94–4.99% held-out error; full uncertainty coverage remains open. Pass848 combines the public supply-coupled detector before four-path traffic, independent wideband RF, autonomous sampled clocks, shared ADC/DAC reference loads and a16-word host pause. Both32-frame cases pass with3.785%/4.945% held-out error; this finite candidate screen does not close whole-chip uncertainty or all supported controls. Pass874/875 fractional wideband against an ideal tuned reference passes four carrier/mode cases at7.38–8.03% with20/30MHz carrier-relative blockers. Fixed-laboratory in-band interference failures remain archived. Broader channel/noise/uncertainty coverage and physical validation remain open.

Finite converter pipelines, shared/separate reference loads and signed ADC clipping diagnostics are integrated. Saturated codes retain validity; nonfinite inputs are rejected. Hardware diagnostic mapping, overload recovery, DAC analog limits and full reference/source-sink/noise operating envelopes remain open. A configurable sampled ADC overload-memory law is now integrated after reference loading; four signed both-mode cases recover and deliver256 samples each. Recovery time/gain are assumed; between-sample overload and physical common-mode behavior remain unknown. Pass848 combines the public supply-coupled detector before four-path traffic, independent wideband RF, autonomous sampled clocks, shared ADC/DAC reference loads and a16-word host pause. Both32-frame cases pass with3.785%/4.945% held-out error; this finite candidate screen does not close whole-chip uncertainty or all supported controls.

Autonomous wired timing, TX shaping and live RX equalization are connected. ReceiverDetectChip now adds two-leg RC receiver detection, timed commands, TX exclusion, release, reset/rearm and discoverable interlock state. Known small-coupling-capacitor false negatives require the declared load envelope. Probe supply coupling, broader uncertainty, equalizer calibration and automatic slip reporting remain open. SupplyDetectChip now feeds an assumed positive-current/bias/sink-overhead load into the actual shared RC rail and oscillator pulling; both-mode finite RF capture and timestep refinement pass. Rail feedback into probe stimulus/sensors remains open. Signed probe-drive gain and sensor-offset dependence on the actual rail now pass both-mode nominal-load and refinement checks. Release now uses a4us minimum dwell plus a local5mV monitor criterion; baseline also uses only the local sensor. Sixteen load histories and stuck-monitor timeout pass. Arbitrary precharged remote networks and full sensor/timing uncertainty remain unqualified.

Management now discovers six existing converter/memory/wired engines and returns actual configured owner, scheduled/in-flight busy and armed/frozen flags. Both-mode tests exercise ownership conflicts and apply-time snapshots. Full analog tile/diagnostic resource graph, trim-to-analog calibration, atomic multi-resource configuration and asynchronous reset remain open. Model-management IDs are not a frozen SPI ABI. Shutdown tests verify conversion cancellation, disabled wired RX status and configuration freeze until drain acknowledgement; queued TX words now count as busy. Pass852 adds a standalone two-input weighted gm/C tile with leakage, saturation and hysteresis; analytical/state tests pass. Diagnostic mux, ADC ownership and timed configuration integration remain open. Pass853 DiagnosticChip connects tile output to the I-ADC with exclusive pair allocation, finite conversion/host transport, reference loading and discoverable ownership. Four cases pass; timed management, internal monitor sources and common top integration remain open. Pass854 adds timed tile weight/enable, diagnostic select, discharge and status commands with execution-time permission and epoch fences. Physical monitor sources, triggers and common top integration remain open. Pass856 common entry adds timed internal monitor selection with fixed-cadence rail/reference observations feeding the tile and ADC. Both-mode transport and subdivision tests pass; pad sensing, shutdown/rearm and physical buffer behavior remain unqualified. Pass857 monitor status is epoch-qualified and invalidated on shutdown. Both-mode probe-pad monitoring, stopped updates, retained analog state and opposite-mode rearm pass. Physical buffer behavior, freshness limits and trigger routing remain open.

Timed transactions configure resources and start finite32-sample local TX/RX atomically with a signed programmable relative converter offset. Both-mode simultaneous/leading/lagging starts and atomic past-start rejection pass. Continuous streaming/run-stop, external trigger routing, LO/trim/calibration and hardware SPI/CDC mapping remain open. configure_rf_carrier now accepts integer-Hz targets in the declared2.3–2.5GHz command envelope, only while reset/disarmed; this envelope is not a physical tuning guarantee. Pass858 adds timed count-free RX in the common entry, bounded streaming codec state, duplicate-start rejection, explicit abort stop and overflow fault/drain tests in both modes. Continuous TX, lossless stop and independent host agreement remain open. Pass859 adds timed count-free host TX through existing framed input, DAC queue and pipeline; both-mode exact sequence, stop and underrun tests pass. Atomic dual-start, triggers, lossless stop and rate uncertainty remain open. Pass860 adds atomic timed continuous TX/RX start with signed relative timing and both-mode rejection tests for busy or past-start conflicts. Trigger routing and lossless stop remain open.

Both host buses now drive continuous shared-rail RF/wired oscillator frequency pulling in the connected controller. Small signed sensitivities preserve transport; excessive values fault; independent RF analog samples expose coupling. Internal switching currents, separate domains/package networks and combined-profile wideband quality/uncertainty with these clocks remain open. Receiver-detect drive/release loading now produces shared-rail droop and measurable independent RF changes under an explicit driver-current law. Two-way probe supply sensitivity and a full uncertainty envelope remain open.

The archived pass842 aggregate passed80 scenarios with649 source hashes and80 report/log hash pairs verified.107 scenarios are now registered, including the public detector entry and combined independent-wideband test. Later isolated passes do not constitute a fresh aggregate. Whole-chip closure and physical qualification remain unproven. Runner now honors explicit failure/quality flags and hashes all candidate top profiles; no fresh aggregate has been run.

not_deferred: Missing functional blocks and control paths from the intended architecture
Unbounded persistent rate mismatch disguised by short runs
Silent loss, stale data, impossible event ordering or invalid-state continuation
Explicit parameter envelopes and tests on both sides of uncertainty
